question: Do consumer guarantee rights end when the manufacturer's warranty expires?

expected.answer:
Relevant passages from the local corpus (answerability has not been verified):

A warranty is an extra promise voluntarily offered when selling goods or services. Once given, the business must honour it. A warranty against defects supplements consumer guarantees rather than replacing them. Expiry of a manufacturer's warranty does not automatically end consumer guarantee rights; acceptable quality rights may continue, depending on the circumstances. Businesses must not suggest that consumer rights end with the warranty period. Extended warranties are optional and usually cost extra. They may provide no additional rights beyond automatic consumer guarantees. Businesses should explain the extra benefits and must not pressure customers or mislead them into buying rights they already have. [1]

Acceptable quality includes safety, durability, freedom from defects, satisfactory appearance, and suitability for the normal uses of similar products. A product must suit a particular purpose communicated to the business or advertised, subject to exceptions such as unreasonable reliance or buying despite a warning that it will not suit that purpose. Services must be performed with reasonable care and skill. When no completion time was agreed, services must be supplied within a reasonable time.
